subject: Maths
title: 2 times table
subtitle: Multiplication and Division (2, 5, 10 Times Tables) · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can recall and use the 2 times table to multiply and divide.

key_vocab.definition: The 2 times table is a list of multiples of 2: numbers we get when we count in 2s. Numbers in the 2 times table are always even.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can recall and use the 2 times table to multiply and divide.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: 2 times table -- The 2 times table is a list of multiples of 2: numbers we get when we count in 2s. Numbers in the 2 times table are always even.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. 2 × 4 means ‘4 groups of 2’. You can also think of it as ‘2 groups of 4’ — the answer is the same.
2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 2×4 = 8
Four groups of 2

Key examples:
  ✓ 1 × 2 = 2  (starting point)
  ✓ 2 × 2 = 4  (double)
  ✓ 5 × 2 = 10  (halfway to 10)
  ✗ 3 × 2 = 7  (wrong)
  ✗ 2 × 0 = 2  (any × 0 = 0)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single multiplication
  Calculate 5 × 2
  5 groups of 2
  2 + 2 + 2 + 2  ...
  = 10
  = 10
  (Skip-count in 2s 5 times to reach 10.)

Example 2 – missing factor
  Solve: ___ × 2 = 8
  How many 2s in 8?
  Count up: 2, 4, 6, ...
  = 4
  = 4
  (Divide: 8 ÷ 2 = 4.)
